prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Brazilian star Kaka is leading the campaign for David Beckham to stay at Italian giants AC Milan beyond his agreed loan spell. Former England captain David Beckham has made an immediate impact with his contribution at AC Milan. The England midfielder is due to return to the Los Angeles Galaxy in March but  playmaker Kaka said Beckham had already shown his star qualities. The 33-year-old played 89 minutes of the 2-2 draw with Roma on Sunday following a friendly outing against Hamburg. "David has shown that he is a player ready to run the extra mile," Kaka told a news conference in Zurich ahead of FIFA's world player of the year gala. "The first matches showed quite clearly what his qualities are and his passing ability and his capacity to play well. "Perhaps these first two months will lead to six months or to one year, to more contracts. I certainly would like to play more with him." Beckham's advisers have stressed that there are no plans for him to stay at AC Milan beyond March 9. However, former Galaxy general manager Alexi Lalas last week expressed fears that Beckham could be tempted to bring an early end to his time in the U.S. AC Milan coach Carlo Ancelotti revealed Beckham's attitude and intelligence had won him a place in the starting side in Rome where he had been expected to start on the bench. "He did well," said Ancelotti. "I chose Beckham to start because he proved in recent days to be a very intelligent player and serious. "The appearance against Roma is a small reward for him because he worked very hard and has adapted well to the team. "This was only his second game with us and he will improve. I believe everyone is happy to have Beckham here." Dutch midfielder Clarence Seedorf said: "We have to compliment him. He has done a good job and he grew in the game. He still needs to improve but I think he can be very satisfied with what he has done after two months of not playing." Roma stand-in captain Daniele De Rossi suggested Milan had made a shrewd move in capturing the 33-year-old. "From a media standpoint Beckham is impressive," De Rossi said. "He is a nice guy, has a beautiful wife, has won so many trophies in his career and perhaps this penalises him as a player although I believe he has the feet and the determination." Beckham, meanwhile, forecast that Sunday's double goalscorer Alexandre Pato of Brazil is destined for greatness. "I have seen him in training and on the pitch. He is only 19 years of age and I think he can become one of the greatest players in the world," said Beckham. Milan are nine points behind Serie A leaders Inter going into Saturday's home game against Fiorentina with Beckham seemingly set to retain his starting slot.

(CNN) -- Brazilian star Kaká is leading calls for David Beckham to remain with Italian giants AC Milan beyond his agreed loan spell.

Former England captain Beckham has made an immediate impact since joining Milan. The midfielder is due to return to the Los Angeles Galaxy in March, but playmaker Kaká said Beckham had already demonstrated his star qualities.

The 33-year-old played 89 minutes in Sunday’s 2-2 draw with Roma after featuring in a friendly against Hamburg.

“David has shown that he is a player ready to run the extra mile,” Kaká told a news conference in Zurich ahead of FIFA’s World Player of the Year gala.

“The first matches showed quite clearly what his qualities are, as well as his passing ability and his capacity to play well.

“Perhaps these first two months will lead to six months, one year or more contracts. I certainly would like to play more with him.”

Beckham’s advisers have stressed that there are no plans for him to remain at AC Milan beyond March 9. However, former Galaxy general manager Alexi Lalas last week expressed concern that Beckham could be tempted to bring his time in the United States to an early end.

AC Milan coach Carlo Ancelotti revealed that Beckham’s attitude and intelligence had earned him a place in the starting lineup against Roma, despite expectations that he would begin the match on the bench.

“He did well,” Ancelotti said. “I chose Beckham to start because, in recent days, he proved himself to be a very intelligent and serious player.

“The appearance against Roma is a small reward for him because he worked very hard and has adapted well to the team.

“This was only his second game with us, and he will improve. I believe everyone is happy to have Beckham here.”

Dutch midfielder Clarence Seedorf said: “We have to compliment him. He has done a good job, and he grew into the game. He still needs to improve, but I think he can be very satisfied with what he has done after two months without playing.”

Roma stand-in captain Daniele De Rossi suggested Milan had made a shrewd move by securing the 33-year-old.

“From a media standpoint, Beckham is impressive,” De Rossi said. “He is a nice guy, has a beautiful wife, has won so many trophies in his career, and perhaps this penalizes him as a player, although I believe he has the feet and the determination.”

Meanwhile, Beckham predicted that Sunday’s two-goal scorer, Brazil’s Alexandre Pato, is destined for greatness.

“I have seen him in training and on the pitch. He is only 19 years of age, and I think he can become one of the greatest players in the world,” Beckham said.

Milan are nine points behind Serie A leaders Inter ahead of Saturday’s home match against Fiorentina, with Beckham seemingly set to retain his place in the starting lineup.

Beckham, the former England captain, quickly made his presence felt after joining the Italian club. Although the midfielder is expected to return to the Los Angeles Galaxy in March, Kaka believes he has already demonstrated the qualities that made him a global star.

After appearing in a friendly against Hamburg, the 33-year-old played 89 minutes in Milan’s 2-2 draw with Roma on Sunday.

Speaking in Zurich before FIFA’s World Player of the Year ceremony, Kaka praised Beckham’s commitment, passing and overall ability. He said the Englishman had proved willing to make an exceptional effort and that his first games had clearly displayed what he could offer.

Kaka also suggested that the initial two-month arrangement might eventually be extended to six months, a year or even further contracts, adding that he would welcome the opportunity to spend more time playing alongside Beckham.

Beckham’s representatives, however, have insisted that he does not intend to remain with Milan after March 9. Despite that, former Galaxy general manager Alexi Lalas said last week that he was concerned Beckham might be persuaded to end his career in the United States earlier than planned.

Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti said Beckham earned a place in the starting lineup against Roma through his professionalism and tactical awareness, even though he had initially been expected to begin the match on the substitutes’ bench.

Ancelotti described Beckham’s performance as good and explained that he selected him after observing in recent days how serious and intelligent a player he was. The coach called the Roma appearance a modest reward for Beckham’s hard work and successful adjustment to the team.

He added that, because it was only Beckham’s second match for the club, further improvement should be expected, while also saying that everyone appeared pleased to have him at Milan.

Dutch midfielder Clarence Seedorf likewise praised Beckham’s display. He said his teammate deserved credit for doing well and becoming increasingly influential as the game progressed. Seedorf acknowledged that Beckham still had room to improve but felt he could be highly satisfied with the performance after going two months without playing.

Roma’s acting captain, Daniele De Rossi, indicated that Milan had made a clever decision by signing the 33-year-old. He noted Beckham’s enormous media appeal, describing him as a likable man with a beautiful wife and a career filled with trophies. De Rossi suggested those factors might cause people to undervalue Beckham as a footballer, even though, in his view, the midfielder possessed both technical skill and determination.

Beckham, meanwhile, predicted a brilliant future for Brazilian forward Alexandre Pato, who scored both of Milan’s goals on Sunday. Having watched him in training and in matches, Beckham said the 19-year-old had the potential to develop into one of the finest players in the world.

Ahead of Saturday’s home fixture against Fiorentina, Milan sit nine points behind Serie A leaders Inter, and Beckham appears likely to keep his place in the starting team.

The coach valued his ability to retain possession, deliver accurately from wide areas and protect the team’s shape. As Beckham continued to play well, Ancelotti openly supported extending the loan beyond its original March end date.

Seedorf also emphasized Beckham’s humility and professionalism. He noted that, despite his celebrity, Beckham trained seriously, adapted quickly and behaved as part of the group rather than demanding special treatment. For Milan’s senior players, that attitude was as important as his crossing and set-piece ability.
